prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A clamping device (300) for a light guide (112) is provided. The clamping device (300) includes a carrier structure having a first securing element (301) for securing the light guide (112) in a first position (401), and a second securing element (302) at a distance from the first securing element (301) for securing the light guide (112) in a second position (402), wherein the first and second positions (401, 402) have a first distance (403) in a longitudinal extension of the light guide (112). Further, an intermediate carrier (500) having a first surface (503) on which the first and second securing elements (301, 302) are attached in respective securing positions (501, 502), and an opposing second surface (504), which can be applied to a measurement object, is provided. Hereby, a second distance (505) of the securing positions (501, 502) of the securing elements (301, 302) on the intermediate carrier (500) is greater than the first distance (403) in a longitudinal direction of the light guide (112).

A clamp assembly (300) for retaining a light guide (112) is disclosed. The assembly (300) comprises a support structure with a first fastening member (301) configured to hold the light guide (112) at a first location (401), and a second fastening member (302), spaced apart from the first fastening member (301), configured to hold the light guide (112) at a second location (402). The first and second locations (401, 402) are separated by a first spacing (403) measured along the longitudinal extent of the light guide (112).

The assembly further includes an intermediate support (500) having a first face (503), to which the first and second fastening members (301, 302) are mounted at corresponding attachment locations (501, 502), and an opposite second face (504) configured for placement against a measurement object. The attachment locations (501, 502) on the intermediate support (500) are separated by a second spacing (505) that exceeds the first spacing (403) in the longitudinal direction of the light guide (112).
outputs.L3:
A clamping device is provided for securing a light guide to a measurement object. The device comprises a carrier structure having first and second securing elements arranged at a distance from one another. The securing elements are configured to hold the light guide at respective first and second securing positions, which are separated along the light guide by a first longitudinal distance.

The carrier structure further includes an intermediate carrier having a first surface on which the first and second securing elements are supported and an opposing second surface configured to be applied to the measurement object. The spacing between the securing elements on the intermediate carrier is greater than the first longitudinal distance between the corresponding securing positions on the light guide. As a result, the portion of the light guide extending between the securing positions can be retained in a defined configuration when the clamping device is applied to the measurement object.
outputs.L4:
A clamping device is provided for securing a light guide, such as an optical fiber, in a defined position relative to a measurement object. The device comprises an intermediate carrier configured to contact or be mounted on the measurement object. At least two securing elements are arranged on the intermediate carrier at positions spaced apart in the longitudinal direction of the light guide. Each securing element receives and retains a corresponding portion of the light guide, thereby fixing the light guide at two longitudinally separated securing positions.

The distance between the securing elements on the intermediate carrier is greater than the distance, measured along the light guide before installation, between the portions intended to be retained by those securing elements. As a result, attachment of the light guide to both securing elements places the section extending between them in a controlled installed state. Depending on the configuration, this arrangement may tension, straighten, preload, or otherwise define the position of the light guide relative to the intermediate carrier and the measurement object.

The securing elements may be formed as clamps, clips, grooves, brackets, adhesive retainers, or other structures capable of holding the light guide without impairing its optical function. At least one securing element may be movable or releasable to facilitate installation and adjustment. The intermediate carrier may be rigid or flexible and may be shaped to conform to a surface of the measurement object. It can be attached to the object permanently or removably, for example by mechanical fastening, clamping, bonding, or magnetic coupling.

During installation, a first portion of the light guide is fixed to a first securing element. A second portion is then positioned at and fixed to the second securing element. Because the securing elements are separated by a greater distance than the corresponding selected positions along the uninstalled light guide, the light guide is brought into the desired controlled condition as it is secured. This defined positioning improves repeatability and helps maintain reliable optical coupling or sensing conditions during measurement.

The clamping device is particularly suitable for applications in which a light guide is used to detect strain, deformation, temperature, vibration, displacement, or other properties of a measurement object. By transferring forces or movements from the measurement object through the intermediate carrier to the secured light guide, the device enables accurate and reproducible measurements while protecting the light guide and simplifying its attachment and replacement.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a clamping device that secures a light guide at two longitudinal positions using securing elements mounted farther apart on an intermediate carrier than the corresponding secured points on the light guide.
counterfactuals.output: A clamping device for securing a light guide comprises an intermediate carrier and first and second securing elements supported by the intermediate carrier at mutually spaced longitudinal positions. The securing elements engage respective first and second secured points of the light guide. A spacing between the securing elements on the intermediate carrier is greater than a spacing between the corresponding secured points on the light guide. Upon engagement, the spacing difference causes the light guide and/or the intermediate carrier to elastically deform, thereby generating a clamping preload that retains the light guide at the two longitudinal positions. The arrangement provides stable positioning of the light guide while accommodating dimensional tolerances and reducing the need for additional fastening components.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise technical description of a light-guide clamp, preserving reference numerals 300, 112, 301, 302, 401–403, and 500–505, and explaining the relationship between the two relevant distances.
counterfactuals.output: The light-guide clamp 300 secures the light guide 112 between opposing clamp portions 301 and 302. Retaining features 401, 402, and 403 position the light guide 112, while dimensions 500, 501, 502, and 503 define the clamp and retaining-feature geometry. Distance 504 is the unclamped spacing between portions 301 and 302, and distance 505 is the corresponding width of the light guide 112. Distance 504 is smaller than distance 505, producing an interference fit that elastically grips the light guide 112.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following invention concept into formal patent language: two spaced securing elements hold a light guide at first and second positions; the elements are attached to one surface of an intermediate carrier whose opposite surface contacts a measurement object; and the mounting-point distance exceeds the distance between the held positions along the light guide.
counterfactuals.output:
A light-guide mounting assembly comprising:

an intermediate carrier having a first surface and an opposite second surface configured to contact a measurement object;

a first securing element and a second securing element disposed in spaced-apart relation and attached to the first surface of the intermediate carrier; and

a light guide retained by the first and second securing elements at respective first and second holding positions,

wherein a distance between respective mounting points at which the first and second securing elements are attached to the intermediate carrier is greater than a distance, measured along the light guide, between the first and second holding positions.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent abstract for an optical sensing assembly’s clamping device, including a carrier structure, first and second securing elements, an intermediate carrier, a measurement-object contact surface, and unequal spacing between the securing positions and the light-guide clamping positions.
counterfactuals.output: A clamping device for an optical sensing assembly includes a carrier structure, a first securing element, and a second securing element arranged to secure an intermediate carrier to the carrier structure at respective first and second securing positions. The intermediate carrier supports at least one light guide and includes a measurement-object contact surface configured to be positioned relative to a measurement object. The first and second securing elements cooperate with the intermediate carrier to clamp the light guide at respective first and second light-guide clamping positions. A spacing between the first and second securing positions differs from a spacing between the first and second light-guide clamping positions. The unequal spacing produces a defined deformation or preload of the intermediate carrier, thereby controlling the position and contact force of the measurement-object contact surface and stabilizing optical coupling between the light guide and the measurement object.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in one patent-style paragraph, a device that creates slack or curvature in a light guide by mounting two clamps on a carrier at a greater separation than the longitudinal distance between the corresponding secured locations on the light guide.
counterfactuals.output: A light-guide assembly comprising a carrier, a first clamp mounted to the carrier at a first position, and a second clamp mounted to the carrier at a second position spaced from the first position by a carrier separation distance, wherein the first and second clamps are configured to secure respective first and second locations of a light guide having a longitudinal distance therebetween that is less than the carrier separation distance, such that, upon securing the first and second locations to the respective clamps, an intermediate portion of the light guide is displaced from a straight path and forms a predetermined slack, bend, or curved profile between the clamps.
